hero.title: Quiet battery care
hero.jp: 静かに見守り、無理なく長持ち。
hero.body: Your MacBook battery wears down a little with every full charge. Battery Sensei watches the details: warns before shutdown, holds a healthier charge limit, and shows which apps drain power, how cycles add up, and whether capacity is aging normally.
hero.menuCaption: Lives in your menu bar. Speaks only when it matters.

featured.title: Low-battery alerts, your way.
featured.italic: Zen, regular, or hard to miss.
featured.body: macOS shows a percentage. Sensei reads what that number means, so you get the right nudge before your MacBook dies. Use the three presets, or set your own thresholds and dismiss times.

handoffs.title: A quiet update when power changes.
handoffs.italic: Time left when you unplug. Time to your limit when you connect.
handoffs.body: Turn either update on or off. After unplugging, Sensei starts with your recent workload and refines the battery estimate live. After plugging in, it waits for charging to settle, then shows the time to your active charge limit, or 100% in Travel Mode. Both stay out of the way and close with Escape.

chargeLimit.title: Charge limit
chargeLimit.body: Lithium-ion batteries age faster when they sit at 100%. Pick a cap (80% is the gentle default); Sensei holds it in the background. Flying tomorrow? One tap tops up to 100%, then your cap returns after the trip.

glance.title: One glance, the whole story
glance.body: Charge, source, watts in or out, time left. The whole picture at a glance. No dock icon. No notification noise. Nothing to click unless you want to. Stay current without checking twice.

meetings.title: Meetings, met.

travel-mode.heading: Travel Mode.
travel-mode.headingItalic: Full charge for the trip. Back to your cap after.
travel-mode.body: Sensei normally holds your charge at the cap you set (80% suggested) so the battery ages slower. The night before a flight, tap Travel Mode. Sensei lifts the cap, charges to 100%, switches to stricter low-battery warnings (30% / 15% / 5%), and pauses Apple's Optimized Battery Charging. The next morning at 9 AM your normal limit comes back automatically. No reminder to undo it. No battery sitting at 100% for weeks.
travel-mode.mockupCaption: Limit lifted to 100%. Auto-resets tomorrow at 9 AM.
travel-mode.why: Lithium-ion batteries age faster when held at 100%. A typical "top up before a trip and forget" leaves a MacBook at full charge for weeks, measurably aging the cells. The 9 AM auto-reset is the safety net: even if you forget, the cap returns.

custom-thresholds.heading: Custom thresholds.
custom-thresholds.body: The three included presets cover most days, but if you want 22% Warning for 14 s and 6% Alert until acknowledged, you can build exactly that. Sensei lets you set the exact percent for each escalation level and how long each card stays on screen. Per-tier, not one global number.
custom-thresholds.mockupCaption: Info · Warning · Alert. Each with its own percent and dismiss time.
custom-thresholds.why: One global warning threshold can't serve someone on a long-haul flight and someone in back-to-back meetings the same way. Per-tier thresholds let the nudges fit the day.

alert-presets.heading: Alert presets.
alert-presets.headingItalic: Zen Mode. Regular Mode. Teach Me Senpai.
alert-presets.body: Zen Mode whispers at 15% (closes in 5 s) and once more at 5% (10 s), quiet enough to let you finish. Regular Mode adds a red overlay at 5% and a persistent alert at 2%. Teach Me Senpai keeps it simple but stern: a red overlay at 15% and a full-screen alert at 5%, both staying until you dismiss. Pick the mood that fits, or compose your own with Custom thresholds.
alert-presets.mockupCaption: Three preset moods. One tap to switch, any time.
alert-presets.why: macOS gives you exactly one battery notification: at 10%. By then it's often too late for the slide you were about to ship. Three presets let the warning match the stakes.

battery-journal.heading: Saga: your MacBook battery history.
battery-journal.headingItalic: Cycles, charges, rescues, all in context.
battery-journal.body: Saga is the long view of your battery's life. A charge history chart you can flip between 24 h / 3 d / 7 d, a Battery Health panel (capacity, cycles, temperature, condition), the top power-hungry apps right now or over the last 3 hours / 5 days, and Wrapped-style Weekly + Monthly recaps. When you rescue a battery in time (plug in within 30 minutes of a critical warning), Sensei creates a Rescue Receipt: a small, shareable card to mark the save.
battery-journal.mockupCaption: Lifetime stats, charge history, Wrapped recaps. All on the Saga page.
battery-journal.why: Battery numbers without context are just numbers. "92% capacity" tells you nothing. Saga gives the same number a story: what it looked like a week ago, which apps cost it the most, which day you nearly lost it.

meeting-battery-guard.heading: Meeting Guard.
meeting-battery-guard.headingItalic: Know before your battery becomes the problem.
meeting-battery-guard.body: A Pro feature. Included in the free trial, then unlocked by Lifetime or Yearly Patron. Opt-in. Sensei reads the next 4 hours of calendar events on-device (EventKit, default lookahead). It scores each meeting against your current battery (Comfortable, Tight, Critical, or Catastrophic) and only nudges when it should. Critical: 30 / 15 / 5 / 1 min before, with the exact minute the laptop would die and the fix ("22 min on the charger and it lasts through the meeting"). Catastrophic: warned immediately. Tight: a single 30-min nudge. Comfortable: silent. Plug in early enough and pending warnings cancel themselves. Titles stay readable in notifications by default; one toggle redacts them.
meeting-battery-guard.mockupCaption: 4-hour lookahead. Only nudges when it should.
meeting-battery-guard.why: A 10% warning mid-meeting is useless: you can't leave to find a charger. Reading your calendar lets Sensei warn you when there's still time to fix it, and stay silent the rest of the time.

energy-usage.heading: Per-app battery drain.
energy-usage.headingItalic: See which apps cost the most.
energy-usage.body: On the Saga page, Sensei ranks the top power users. Flip between right now (live), the last 3 hours, or 5 days, and toggle each value between percent of a full battery and watts (live draw) or watt-hours (over a window). Each app gets an Activity-Monitor-style energy impact score (CPU time blended with idle wake-ups), an impact label (Low / Moderate / High / Very high), and a search filter so you can find every Chrome helper in the list. History is sampled every 5 minutes; the live Now view refreshes about every 10 seconds. No system extension, no kernel hooks.
energy-usage.mockupCaption: Top apps · Now / 3h / 5d · percent or watts. Live view refreshed ~10 s.
energy-usage.why: Battery loss is almost never the battery's fault. It's a hung helper, a sleepless tab, a video call that won't release the GPU. Knowing which app costs you the most is the difference between a 4-hour day and a 7-hour day.

low-power-mode.heading: Low Power Mode,
low-power-mode.headingItalic: without remembering to turn it on.
low-power-mode.body: macOS hides Low Power Mode three panes deep in System Settings. Battery Sensei turns it into a rule: pick a battery percentage or a time-remaining trigger, and the mode switches on when you cross it, then off again when you plug in. Apple's setting does the throttling. Sensei just remembers for you.
low-power-mode.mockupCaption: One trigger, both directions: on when you cross it, off when you charge.
low-power-mode.why: You never think of Low Power Mode at the right moment. 18% left, a meeting starting, no charger in the bag. That is exactly when it's furthest from your mind. Set the rule once on a calm afternoon and it covers every bad one after it. Because it switches back off on its own, you won't find your Mac still throttled a week later.

power-flow.heading: Where your watts go,
power-flow.body: Three numbers macOS never shows side by side: what the charger delivers, what reaches the battery, and what your Mac draws. Unplugged, that last number is your discharge rate. No estimate. The actual reading.
power-flow.mockupCaption: Adapter in, system draw, battery flow.
power-flow.why: A percentage can't tell you why it's falling. Watts can. Once you see your 96 W charger delivering 38 W through a bad cable, or the system eating everything the adapter sends, the mystery is over.

system-load.heading: Why the battery is dropping:
system-load.body: CPU, GPU, memory pressure, and disk I/O, right beside your battery numbers. When the battery drains fast, one of these four usually explains it: a pinned core, a busy GPU, a sync client writing all afternoon.
system-load.mockupCaption: CPU, GPU, memory pressure, and disk I/O, sampled together.
system-load.why: “It died fast today” is a feeling. Load is evidence. The system panel shows that something is working your Mac; the app energy panel names it. Together they turn a bad battery day into a process you can quit.

charge-limit.heading: A daily charge cap,
charge-limit.headingItalic: and a weekly cycle to keep it honest.
charge-limit.body: Lithium-ion wears fastest at the extremes, and hours parked at 100% are the part you control. Set a daily cap and charging stops there. Once a week, Sensei suggests a fuller cycle so the runtime estimate stays honest.
charge-limit.mockupCaption: Set the cap; Sensei reminds you about the weekly calibration cycle.
charge-limit.why: You can't repair a battery, but you can slow the wear. A cap trades runtime you weren't using for capacity you'll want in two years. The weekly cycle keeps the gauge calibrated, so you can watch the trade pay off.

battery-health.heading: Capacity, cycles, condition,
battery-health.body: The three numbers macOS keeps but rarely shows: how much the pack holds today, how many full cycles it has behind it, and Apple's own condition verdict, unedited, beside the charging habits that shaped them.
battery-health.mockupCaption: Capacity, condition, cycle count. Read straight from the pack.
battery-health.why: “92% capacity” means nothing on its own. Fine for a three-year-old Mac, alarming for a new one. Health is a trend, not a score, which is why these numbers live next to your charge history instead of on their own.

statistics.heading: Your battery week,
statistics.body: Time unplugged, charge sessions, average discharge depth, the hottest stretch, the rescues that landed in time, folded into weekly and monthly recaps you can read in twenty seconds.
statistics.mockupCaption: Weekly and monthly recaps, computed on your Mac.
statistics.why: The live percentage answers “what now”. It never answers “is this normal for me”. Recaps show the pattern (the travel week, the month a sync client ran wild) while there's still time to change it.

honors.heading: Habits worth keeping,
honors.body: Honors mark the habits that actually help a battery: steady charge ranges, rescues before the crash, streaks that survive a busy week. No points, no leaderboard, no reminders.
honors.mockupCaption: Earned quietly, from your own history.
honors.why: Cycle count only goes up and capacity only goes down. Habits are the one lever you hold, and habits respond to feedback. Honors are the quietest feedback that still works: there when you look, silent when you don't.

general.heading: Short settings,
general.body: Menu-bar content, appearance, language, start at login. No cloud sync or app telemetry: Sensei does not upload battery, calendar, or per-app energy data. Network use is limited to updates, licensing, and support or feature actions you start.
general.why: Most settings screens grow into a second job. This one stays short on purpose. Sensitive app data lives on your Mac, so the main decisions are how Sensei looks and when it starts. Its few network services stay narrow and explicit.

items.q: How does the charge limit work?
a: Sensei stops the charge at the level you pick. Default is **80%**: cooler battery, longer life.

items.q: Does Sensei send my data anywhere?
a: **Your sensitive app data stays local.**

Sensei has no app telemetry, analytics SDK, crash reporter, or cloud account. Battery history, calendar titles, and per-app energy readings stay on your Mac. Updates, licensing, and feature or support actions you start use the named services in our Privacy notice.

items.q: How is Battery Sensei different from the macOS battery menu?
a: macOS shows a percentage. **Sensei watches what that percentage means.**
Smart low-battery alerts at thresholds you choose. A charge limit with Travel Mode. Live charging watts. Cycle and capacity over time.
Plus a calm, plain-English history of how your battery is aging.

items.q: How much battery does Sensei itself use?
a: **Less than 1%.**
Native AppKit and SwiftUI. No background polling. Sensei samples only when macOS reports a change.

items.q: Is Battery Sensei an AlDente alternative?
a: **Yes.** If you want charge limits plus smart warnings and battery history, Sensei is an AlDente alternative.
Ships as one notarized .pkg installer. Pro adds Meeting Guard, unlimited history, and custom warning rules. With Lifetime, one payment unlocks Pro for good.
Side-by-side comparison lives in the Compare section above.

items.q: How do I update Battery Sensei?
a: Sensei checks for updates on launch.
A new build shows up as a quiet notice. **You install when you say so.** No silent pushes, no nag screens.
Opt-in Pro feature. Sensei reads your calendar locally and predicts which meetings your battery might not survive.
When a meeting is at risk, you get up to four nudges: **30, 15, 5, and 1 minute before** start.
Each nudge names the exact minute the laptop is predicted to die ("dies 17 min into standup") and the plug-in time that fixes it ("22 min on the charger and it lasts through the meeting").
Event titles never leave your Mac. Sensei reads the calendar locally via EventKit. If the risk passes, pending reminders cancel silently.

privacy.title: What we collect.
privacy.intro: Battery Sensei is a privacy-first macOS app from 41BIT LLC. Sensitive battery, calendar, and per-app energy data stays on your Mac. We process the minimum needed for the website, licensing, purchases, email, support, and feature-board actions, with every network service named below.

tldr.heading: The short version

do.1: Keep sensitive battery, calendar, and per-app energy data on your Mac. The app has no telemetry, analytics SDK, crash reporter, or cloud account.
do.2: Measure site use with Vercel's cookieless analytics: aggregate and pseudonymous pageview and performance data, plus the limited custom events named below.
do.3: Keep only data you submit or generate through site actions: signup, contact and feature-request details, pseudonymous votes, limited checkout or licensing references, and referral links you choose to share.
do.4: Use a small, named set of processors and independent controllers for hosting, payments, email, downloads, and licensing.

dont.1: Sell, rent or share your data with advertisers. Ever.
dont.2: Run ad or social-media trackers, embed tracking pixels or sharing widgets, set third-party tracking cookies, or profile you across sites.
dont.3: Build profiles about you or make automated decisions that affect you.
dont.4: Require an account or a login to use the app.

tldr.note: There is no tracking-cookie banner because we set no advertising or cross-site tracking cookies. We do not sell personal data or share it for cross-context behavioral advertising, and we do not use cross-site tracking, so Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control signals cause no different behavior. Website visits and the app's update, licensing, download, and user-triggered support or feature actions contact named services as detailed below.

controller.heading: Who's responsible for your data
controller.p1: Battery Sensei and battery-sensei.app are operated exclusively by <0>41BIT LLC</0>, a Wyoming limited liability company with company address 5830 E 2nd St, Ste 7000 #36418, Casper, Wyoming 82609, United States. 41BIT LLC is the sole app and site operator, the software publisher and distributor, the developer-authorized end-user licensor, and the controller for processing whose purposes and means it determines. The developer, Sandro Thabiso Schaier, separately owns the Software and related intellectual property. Named independent controllers such as Polar and GitHub remain responsible for their own processing. References to "we" / "us" mean 41BIT LLC.
controller.p2: Contact for any privacy-related question, request, or complaint: <0>info@battery-sensei.app</0>. We respond within the period required by applicable law.
controller.p3: 41BIT LLC has designated <0>Sandro Thabiso Schaier</0>, Korunní 2569/108, 101 00 Prague 10, Vinohrady, Czech Republic, as its representative in the European Union under <1>Article 27 GDPR</1>. EU/EEA data subjects and supervisory authorities may contact the representative about 41BIT LLC's processing at <2>info@battery-sensei.app</2> or at the postal address above.
controller.p4: The representative is a privacy contact point only. Sandro Thabiso Schaier is also Battery Sensei's developer and intellectual-property owner, but that separate role does not make him the contracting app or site operator, distributor, seller, end-user licensor, or controller. 41BIT LLC remains solely responsible for those operations and as controller.

app.heading: What the macOS app does on your Mac
app.p1: Battery Sensei's core monitoring runs locally on your Mac. Battery and charging readings, calendar event titles, battery history, and per-app energy readings stay on-device and are not sent to 41BIT LLC or its service providers.
app.p2: The app contains no telemetry, analytics SDK, crash reporter, advertising tracker, or cloud account. Local app data is not used to profile you or measure how you use the app.
app.p3: The app does use the network for specific purposes: it checks the update feed at battery-sensei.app and downloads releases from GitHub; licensing is activated or validated through Polar; and feature requests, votes, or support actions you choose use battery-sensei.app. Those requests expose routine network metadata such as IP address and user-agent and send a license key or content you enter only when needed. Sharing a Battery Sensei card is also user-triggered: the image, caption, and a link containing your persistent app-generated Sensei referral code plus card or campaign parameters are handed to the macOS share service you select, which handles them under its own terms. None of these automatic requests includes your battery history, calendar titles, or per-app energy readings.
app.p4: Settings includes a Delete All Local Data control. It deletes Battery Sensei-controlled local history, preferences, app identity, saved device records, and local license and trial data, then quits the app. It does not delete Polar purchase, activation, or license records; website submissions; macOS permission decisions; or macOS's own charging state and system data.

github.heading: Downloading the app and its updates
github.p1: We host the app's installer and its release notes in a public GitHub repository (<0>github.com/schaier-io/battery-sensei-releases</0>). When you click "Download for Mac", or when the in-app updater installs a new version, your device connects directly to GitHub to fetch the file. No GitHub account is required.
github.p2: Like any web server, GitHub receives your IP address, the file you requested and your browser's user-agent in order to serve the download, and may log that data and set its own cookies if you browse the repository in a browser. For this connection <0>GitHub, Inc.</0> (a Microsoft company) acts as an independent controller under its own privacy statement. We never receive a list of who downloaded the app.
github.p3: GitHub's handling of these requests is governed by the <0>GitHub Privacy Statement</0>. If you open an issue or comment on the repository, whatever you write, along with your GitHub username, is shared with GitHub and is publicly visible.

what.heading: The full list, by surface
what.intro: This section covers battery-sensei.app, checkout, the feature board, and the app's limited network actions. The app does not upload its sensitive local measurements. The website and named services process the following minimum data:

items.localeBody: the first-party <0>bs_locale</0> cookie stores your selected language for one year. Local-storage entries <0>bs_theme</0> and <0>bs:currency</0> store explicit theme and currency choices. <0>bs_board_license</0> stores your license key on this device only if you enter it or receive it after checkout so the board can remember voting access. It is sent only in vote or validation POST bodies, never in a URL, header, or cookie.
items.analyticsBody: Vercel Web Analytics records cookieless aggregate and pseudonymous pageview data using a daily request hash. Vercel Analytics does not retain the raw IP address; data points can include normalized URL or route, referrer, approximate location, device, OS, and browser. Before analytics is sent, we remove every query string and replace the dynamic Sensei code in /from/<id> with a generic route. Vercel Speed Insights records Core Web Vitals. Custom events contain only the purchased tier or referral-card variant, never a checkout id, referral code, campaign parameter, battery value, calendar title, or per-app energy reading. We do not use analytics for advertising or cross-site profiling.
items.signupBody: only if you submit the signup form: email address, page locale, signup source, IP address, user-agent, origin, timestamps, confirmation or unsubscribe state, and Resend contact ids used to manage delivery.
items.contactBody: if you contact us, we store the raw and validated name, email, topic, subject, message, IP address, user-agent, origin, ticket, status, and email-delivery ids. If you submit a feature idea, we similarly store its title, description, email, optional name, locale, source, moderation state, and request metadata; only approved title and description text is public, never submitter identity. For voting, your license key is sent to our server and Polar for validation but is never stored raw. Neon stores a keyed-HMAC voter identifier, the feature-request relation, and the vote IP address, plus a separate time-limited license-validation cache. The vote IP address is cleared after 30 days. The keyed voter/request relation remains while the public entry exists to preserve its vote count and prevent duplicate votes, then is deleted with that entry.
items.checkoutBody: for live price previews, /api/price derives the visitor's two-letter country code from Vercel's IP-country header for currency selection and caching within 41BIT LLC/Vercel. It sends Polar only a representative US, DE, or CZ pricing-region code and the requested currency—not the visitor's IP address or actual country. When you buy, Polar independently collects the contact, billing, tax, payment, device, and purchase data needed for the sale. 41BIT LLC does not receive your full card number. Our server retrieves limited checkout, order, customer-email, product, license, fulfillment, and customer-portal information from Polar to deliver the key and provide support.
items.logsBody: Vercel hosting and server-function logs may contain timestamp, full requested path or URL, query parameters, status, user-agent, IP address, checkout or order references present in a URL or query, and diagnostic details. A request to a shared /from/<id> link can therefore place the persistent Sensei referral code and its card or campaign parameters in these logs even though analytics redacts them. We use logs only for reliability, security, fraud prevention, and abuse investigation. Vercel controls their retention under the current service and account configuration, which may change.

The address remains unsubscribed and receives Battery Sensei release, walkthrough, or product updates only after you click the double-opt-in link. Legal basis: <0>consent</0> (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR where applicable), withdrawable at any time via the unsubscribe link in every update or by writing to <1>info@battery-sensei.app</1>.
items.communicationsBody: responding to contact or support requests, moderating or publishing feature submissions, and sending requested status notices. Legal bases: <0>contract or steps at your request, and legitimate interest</0> (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR where applicable for contract or pre-contract support, and Art. 6(1)(f) for requested communications and product planning).
items.mediaBody: the YouTube connection begins only when you press Play. Legal basis: <0>taking steps at your request to provide the video</0> (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR where applicable). Pressing Play authorizes that connection and playback; we do not describe the click as GDPR consent unless all legal requirements for consent are met.
items.analyticsName: Cookieless analytics, performance and service security
items.analyticsBody: privacy-focused page, performance, conversion, referral, and reliability signals. Legal basis: <0>legitimate interest</0> (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR where applicable) in operating, securing, and improving the service. No advertising retargeting or cross-site profiling.
items.abuseBody: IP, user-agent, origin, rate-limit records, and pseudonymous vote identifiers for signup, contact, feature-board, and licensing actions. Legal basis: <0>legitimate interest</0> (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR where applicable) in protecting the service from spam, scraping, credential probing, and fraud.

why.noAutomated: We do not engage in any automated decision-making or profiling with legal or similarly significant effects on you (Art. 22 GDPR).
why.required: Providing signup, contact, and feature-submission data is optional. Polar checkout details are required to complete a purchase. A license key or activation identifier is required to activate or validate Pro, and a license key is required for licensed feature voting; without the required data, that action cannot be completed. The core free app requires no account.

processors.heading: Who receives or stores data
processors.intro: We use a small set of named providers. Some process data for 41BIT LLC; Polar, GitHub, and Google/YouTube also act as independent controllers for their own customer-facing services. Some processing may occur in the United States or other countries. Where applicable law restricts a transfer, it may proceed only under a lawful mechanism applicable to that provider and destination, such as an adequacy decision or Standard Contractual Clauses. Contact <0>info@battery-sensei.app</0> to request information about, or a copy of, the relevant safeguards, subject to lawful redactions. Each role is described below. We do not sell data or share it with advertising networks.

items.vercelBody: hosts the website, server functions, request logs, Vercel Web Analytics, and Speed Insights. Analytics receives redacted routes, cookieless daily request hashes, and limited event fields; hosting and security logs can still process full referral paths, campaign parameters, and routine connection metadata. Policy: <0>vercel.com/legal/privacy-policy</0>.
items.youtubeBody: the video facade makes no request to YouTube before you press Play. If you press Play, the embedded player loads from youtube-nocookie.com and sends routine connection and device data, such as IP address, user-agent, referrer, and the video request, to Google/YouTube, which acts as an independent controller under its own terms. Policy: <0>policies.google.com/privacy</0>.
items.polarBody: reseller and merchant of record for purchases, and an independent controller for its checkout and customer-facing services. For live price previews, our server sends Polar only a representative US, DE, or CZ pricing-region code and the requested currency, not the visitor's IP address or actual country. Polar handles billing, payment, tax, invoices, refunds, chargebacks, and license issuance; it also validates license keys used by the app and feature board. Polar collects card details directly; 41BIT LLC does not receive the full card number. Policy: <0>polar.sh/legal/privacy-policy</0>.
items.resendBody: our email-delivery processor. It processes recipient addresses, message content, and delivery metadata for double-opt-in confirmations, Battery Sensei release, walkthrough, or product updates, contact confirmations, and feature-board notices. A pending Resend contact exists before confirmation but remains unsubscribed; update emails begin only after confirmation. Policy: <0>resend.com/legal/privacy-policy</0>.
items.postgresBody: our serverless PostgreSQL provider through the Vercel Marketplace. The EU-hosted database stores newsletter, contact, feature-request and moderation records, pseudonymous board votes, license-validation cache entries, and operational rate-limit records. It does not store full card numbers or raw feature-board license keys. Policy: <0>databricks.com/legal/privacynotice</0>.

items.signupBody: unconfirmed pending database records and their Resend contacts are deleted automatically by a daily cleanup once they are 9 days old in total (the 48-hour confirmation period plus 7 days). Confirmed records are kept while you remain subscribed. After you unsubscribe, the Neon record is automatically minimized to the data needed to honor and document the opt-out and prevent accidental re-enrollment. You can request erasure, subject to any minimal suppression or legal record that must be retained.
items.localBody: the app's Delete All Local Data control removes all local data controlled by Battery Sensei and then quits; Polar records, website submissions, macOS permissions, and system state remain outside that local deletion. Website language, theme, currency, and the board license key remain in your browser until you clear or change them; the board key is also removed when the app detects that it is invalid.
items.analyticsBody: retained under the configured retention settings of the applicable Vercel provider account. Those periods may change with the service plan or account configuration.
items.contactBody: private support messages and non-public feature-submission data are deleted automatically 24 months after the last activity, unless a legal hold or legal obligation requires longer preservation. For approved public feature entries, submitter identity and private request metadata are anonymized after 24 months, while the public title, description, and aggregate vote count may remain on the board. Each feature-vote IP address is cleared after 30 days. Its keyed voter hash and request relation remain while the public feature entry exists to preserve the vote count and prevent duplicate votes, then are deleted with that entry. The separate pseudonymous LicenseVoter license-validation cache is deleted after 60 days of inactivity.
items.purchaseBody: Polar, as merchant of record and independent controller, retains transaction, tax-invoice, and license records under its policy and applicable law. 41BIT LLC does not keep a full purchase or license record in Neon; it retrieves records from Polar when needed for delivery or support. The purchase-complete analytics event retains only the tier, not a checkout, order, customer, or license identifier.
items.logsBody: 41BIT-controlled admin login-attempt records are deleted automatically after 30 days. Vercel controls retention of infrastructure request and function logs under its service and account configuration. A specific security incident, legal hold, or legal obligation may require longer preservation.

rights.heading: What you can ask us to do
rights.intro: Depending on where you live and subject to applicable law, you may have the following rights. Where the GDPR applies, these include:

items.access: Request <0>access</0> to the personal data we hold about you (Art. 15 GDPR).
items.correct: Ask us to <0>correct</0> data that is inaccurate or incomplete (Art. 16).
items.delete: Ask us to <0>delete</0> your data when it is no longer needed (Art. 17 GDPR where applicable). Polar may retain transaction and accounting records where applicable law requires it.
items.restrict: Ask us to <0>restrict</0> processing while a correction is being assessed (Art. 18).
items.portable: Receive a <0>portable copy</0> of your data in a machine-readable format (Art. 20).
items.object: <0>Object</0> to processing based on legitimate interest (Art. 21).
items.withdraw: <0>Withdraw consent</0> at any time. The unsubscribe link is at the bottom of every newsletter email.

rights.closing: To exercise any of these rights, email <0>info@battery-sensei.app</0>. We reply within the period required by applicable law. Where the GDPR applies, that is normally one month; complex requests may be extended by up to two further months, in which case we will notify you within the first month and explain why. You may also complain to a competent data-protection authority. Under the GDPR, this includes the authority in your habitual residence, place of work, or place of the alleged infringement; <1>find the relevant authority here</1>.

security.heading: How we protect data
security.p1: We use reasonable technical and organizational measures appropriate to the nature of the data and the risks to protect it. No system or transmission can be guaranteed absolutely secure.

children.heading: Not directed to children
children.p1: Battery Sensei, battery-sensei.app, and the newsletter are not directed to children under 16 or below the applicable local age for independently consenting to this processing. 41BIT LLC does not knowingly collect their personal data. If you are a parent or guardian and believe a child submitted data without valid authorization, contact <0>info@battery-sensei.app</0> so we can review and delete it as required by law.

changes.heading: When this page is updated
changes.p1: When we change a material practice (a new processor, a different retention window, a new type of data collected), we update the date at the top of this page. If a change affects your consent (for example, a new newsletter type), we will email you separately and ask before opting you in.
